title: Maximum Number of Moves in a Grid
summary: Given an m x n matrix with positive integers, starting from any cell in the first column, you can move to adjacent cells in the next column where the value strictly increases.
statement: Given an m x n matrix with positive integers, starting from any cell in the first column, you can move to adjacent cells in the next column where the value strictly increases. Determine the greatest number of such moves possible.
constraints: Start at any cell in the first column.
A move goes to the next column and changes row by -1, 0, or 1, only to a strictly larger value.
Return the greatest possible number of moves.
hints: Represent all rows reachable in the current column as a set.
For each reachable row, test the three bounded neighbor rows in the next column.
If no next row is reachable, the current column index equals the number of completed moves; otherwise continue.
The reachable set is exactly the frontier after each move count, so the last nonempty frontier gives the longest possible path.
editorial: The reachable set is exactly the frontier after each move count, so the last nonempty frontier gives the longest possible path.

tests.explanation: A valid strictly increasing route crosses all four columns, making three moves.
No first-column value can move to a larger adjacent value in column one, so return zero.
